hook: In human brain organoids, MECP2-mutant and healthy cells sort apart and wire together less.
summary: Rett syndrome organoids built from mixed healthy and MECP2-mutant cells showed genotype-dependent spatial patterning, and the two truncating and missense mutations differed. Calcium imaging found that healthy neuron pairs coupled more strongly than mutant or mixed pairs, and RNA sequencing pointed to altered GABA and neurexin-neuroligin signaling. The signaling changes are inferred computationally, and organoids only approximate a real developing brain.
title: Human cortical mosaicoids reveal impact on spatial organization and progressive loss of cross-genotype functional coupling in MECP2 mosaicism
